assessment: The incumbent is adequate for many routine exports: 32/40 had the intended courses, and unchanged-assignment centers had seven-minute median handling. Failures cluster around assignment changes, supporting—but not establishing—a mismatch between current service state and requested-week expectations. Renamed courses in two affected exports limit an assignment-only account: identity matching or timetable disagreement could also matter. The 17-minute overall median and 80% course-set accuracy miss the targets. Zero observed cross-center rows is bounded evidence; the split-course center was absent. Fast execution alongside long replacement waits suggests an operational delay, but elapsed waiting is not measured active handling. All evidence is stipulated synthetic data.

openings.claim: Requested-week course membership may be distorted by applying current instructor assignments; renames may separately create apparent omissions when coordinators compare names.
openings.delta: Distinguishes missing course identities from present courses carrying unexpected names before choosing an export correction.
openings.prediction: With intended course identities held fixed, assignment changes will alter exported membership if the temporal hypothesis holds. Rename-only changes will preserve membership but may trigger coordinator mismatch reports.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, replay unchanged, assignment-change, rename-only and split-course examples. Record exported identities and names; have consenting coordinators identify the intended weekly set. Verify center boundaries and concurrent attendance entry. Reserve the documented CSV unchanged; time-box investigation within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Intended weekly membership can be agreed; historical state availability remains unknown.

openings.claim: Would faster replacement availability materially reduce coordinator handling, or does checking and importing dominate active work?
openings.delta: Separates queue delay from the handling-time success measure.
openings.prediction: A replacement bottleneck will produce repeated request/status work; a checking/import bottleneck will leave substantial active work even when a corrected file is immediately available.
openings.probe: Use the two short sessions per consenting coordinator with fabricated files: counterbalance immediate replacement against the usual request process, timing checking, requesting, downloading and importing separately from waiting.
assumptions: A usability result would guide a bounded change, not establish success across the next 40 exports.
